title: Personal Infinitive after Prepositions
summary: Use personal infinitives after para, antes de, depois de, por, and sem when the subject needs to be explicit.

sections.heading: Para + personal infinitive
sections.body: Use **para** plus personal infinitive to express purpose when the infinitive has its own subject. This is clearer than forcing a subjunctive clause in many contexts.

examples.en: I bought food for you all to eat.

examples.pt: Fale mais devagar para eu entender.
examples.en: Speak more slowly so I can understand.

examples.pt: Deixei a chave aqui para nós entrarmos depois.
examples.en: I left the key here for us to enter later.

sections.heading: Before and after actions
sections.body: After **antes de** and **depois de**, the personal infinitive shows who performs the action, especially when it differs from the main subject.

examples.pt: Antes de você sair, me avise.
examples.en: Before you leave, let me know.

examples.pt: Depois de eles chegarem, vamos jantar.
examples.en: After they arrive, we'll have dinner.

examples.pt: Antes de nós decidirmos, precisamos conversar.
examples.en: Before we decide, we need to talk.

sections.heading: Por and sem
sections.body: With **por** and **sem**, the personal infinitive can express reason, cause, or absence of an action. These structures are common in educated speech and writing.

examples.pt: Por eu morar longe, saio cedo.
examples.en: Because I live far away, I leave early.

keyPoints: Personal infinitive is useful after prepositions with explicit subjects.
Para eu fazer is standard; para mim fazer is nonstandard in careful Portuguese.
Compound personal infinitives use terem, termos, etc.

commonMistakes.note: The subject of the infinitive is eu, not mim.
After por, use infinitive/compound infinitive, not finite past.
